channel.title: Comments on: Why God?

item.title: By: carl
item.dc:creator: carl
item.description:
Kids? When my son Luke was born (at home here) I took him straight away to have a warm bath together. Looking at him,I realized then and there that there was virtually no essential difference between him, age 15 minute or so, and me, age 45.
At that moment I made a major shift from "<em>Not to know yet to think that one knows</em>" over to "<em>To know yet to think that one does not know"</em>. We really are all children, despite what our "thoughts of self" tell us.
Lynn: I ascribe it all genetics as a way of taking "me" out of the picture. If I believed in God, I'd probably be saying it is all as God wills - I am at 'his/her/its' mercy. To put it in a taoist context, "the genetics that can be named/spoken of is not the constant genetics".
Bottom line: We are all mysteriously the same, Christian, Taoist, and everything in between. We just can't help but focus on apparent differences. Belief is simply a way of codifying the differences we 'think we know'... (or so I think ;) ).

item.title: By: Lynn Cornish
item.dc:creator: Lynn Cornish
item.description:
Carl, you make me smile. That you don't expect to be "extremely satisfied" is extremely satisfying to me for some reason.
The connection of "soaking up the moment" is what I consider to be "God" although I'd never use that word. It would be simpler to believe in some organized religion -- who am I to make up my own? -- but it is not in my nature. I swear, I was born without faith, a doubting Thomas. As the Buddha says, trust only your own experience and that's all I can do.
Perhaps it is all genetics.

item.title: By: Dan Littler
item.dc:creator: Dan Littler
item.description: River Wolf, I agree. I've been doing a bit if research into various philosophies and religions recently, and I've come to the conclusion that religion is just philosophy for kids. Take Christianity: the bold characters, God, Jesus, the Holy Spirit, are all allegorical. They're just a way of understanding the underlying philosophies, like teaching kids about fairness/lying/politeness using sock puppets. This is the only difference I've found between philosophy and religion. Both attempt to impart life advice, but religion feels the need to include what I think of as cartoon characters to pass on this advice, as well as a reward/punishment system (eg. Heaven/Hell).

item.title: By: carl
item.dc:creator: carl
item.description:
I more inclined to see this as each person being attracted to that which fits their innate nature. One is born a 'taoist' or a 'christian' (or whatever), whether or not one's environment actually has the particular named models for Taoist or Christian (or whatever). Life experience and circumstances combine with our innate nature to determine how we express what we 'think we know'. I suppose that accounts for the advice, <a href="https://centertao.local/tao-te-ching/dc-lau/#chapter-71" rel="nofollow">To know yet to think that one does not know is best</a>.
Yes, God correlates with female (which is not necessarily have anything to do with women or men). Here's a string of <a href="https://centertao.local/essays/correlations/" rel="nofollow">mutual correlation definition</a> that comes to mind…
Devil= male=something=hard=loud=need=active=bright God = female=nothing=soft=silent=content=passibe=dark

item.title: By: River Wolf
item.dc:creator: River Wolf
item.description:
Great post. Super-male in super-home definitely cuts it.
God is for beginners, and Taoist metaphysics and philosophy is for those with abit more experience.
Even if there was a God, I think there's a higher chance that God is a woman than a man.
